newsitem.title: KENYA: Gunmen free Somali U.N. aid worker in Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen free Somali U.N. aid worker in Mogadishu.

text.p: Gunmen freed unharmed a Somali U.N. aid worker in the Somali capital two days after kidnapping him from his home in southern Mogadishu, U.N. officials said on Saturday.
Robert Hagan, Somalia representative of the World Health Organisation, said 35-year-old Jilani Sheikh Osman, a pharmacist, was released on Friday night by the gunmen who seized him.
"There are rumours money was paid but it is unclear. I have no idea where he was kept. They talked to his family. They did not approach us for anything," Hagan told Reuters in Nairobi.
He said Osman, who ran the Somali central pharmacy in the capital which distributes medicine to hospitals and clinics, was kidnapped from his home in southern Mogadishu on Wednesday night.
Osman was seized in a part of south Mogadishu controlled by supporters of faction leader Hussein Aideed but it was unclear who was behind the abduction. Hagan said the incident was worrying.

Kidnappings and extortion, especially involving staff of foreign aid agencies, are common in Mogadishu, where weapons are easily available and unemployment is extremely high since the departure of the U.N. peacekeeping operation in March 1995.
Somalia has had no central authority since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine who succeeded his father Mohamed Farah Aideed who died on August 1, says he wants to rebuild the ruined infrastructure of Somalia.

Seeking the return of U.N. and other international aid agencies, he met visiting U.N. officials last weekend for the first time since taking over from his father. Most aid agencies pulled out of his south Mogadishu enclave in 1995.
Hussein was elected Somalia's president by supporters but is opposed by other faction leaders who do not recognise his government and control areas bordering on southern Mogadishu.
